## My Thinking

I have farmed this same stretch of land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My back is not what it was at forty, and my two sons are in Shijiazhuang now — they come back for the big harvests if I ask, but day-to-day it is mostly me and my wife.

Here in Quzhou there is really only one sensible thing to do: winter wheat followed by summer maize. Same as my father did it. Same land, two crops a year. I know no other way, and I do not need to. The soil here on the North China Plain is suited for it, we have the irrigation wells, and there is a buyer for both crops at the collection station in town.

I have about 5 mu I still work myself. I stopped renting in the extra plot three years ago — it was too much.

**On wheat (already in the ground, managing it through spring):** I planted in October. I use the Jimai variety — not the old seed I saved myself, I buy improved seed from the village supply co-op. It yields better and has decent resistance to rust. This spring I will give it one topdress of urea at jointing. I irrigated once already before the freeze last autumn and again at jointing. I will do one more irrigation at heading if it does not rain. I will spray once for powdery mildew — the extension station said it was a bad year for it last cycle. Harvest in early June.

**On maize (to be planted June after wheat):** Right after wheat harvest I will direct-seed the maize without turning the soil — saves my back and the county has been saying it protects moisture. I buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, everyone around here uses it, good reason. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and chase with urea at the big bell stage. One or two irrigations unless there is good summer rain. Maybe one pesticide pass for corn borer if I see the signs.

I do not expect miracles. Around 400 kg/mu for wheat and 520 kg/mu for maize is what I usually get. That is enough.
